input.strategy_title: Graduate Llama Stack to General Availability
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Llama Stack shipped as Tech Preview and adoption is strong, but enterprise
customers will not build production GenAI applications on a TP component.
Graduating to GA requires API stability commitments, a production support
posture, and closing the quality gaps that TP status currently excuses. The
full inventory of those gaps is not yet known — TP feedback is scattered across
support tickets, and no systematic GA-readiness assessment has been done.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | A GA-readiness assessment inventories the gaps between current TP quality and GA bar (API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, error handling), producing the definitive GA scope. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Published API surface carries a stability guarantee: versioned APIs, deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade path from the last two TP releases. |
| HLR-3 | P0 | Production support posture is in place: documented SLO targets, backport policy, and supported configuration matrix. |
| HLR-4 | P1 | Safety guardrails via TrustyAI are a supported, documented integration (not an experimental flag) for GA distributions. |
| HLR-5 | P1 | The Dashboard enables Llama Stack management by default for entitled clusters (no TP opt-in gate). |
| HLR-6 | P2 | Documentation is uplifted to GA standards, including migration notes from TP. |

## Affected Components

- Llama Stack
- TrustyAI
- Dashboard

## Out of Scope

- New Llama Stack feature development beyond GA-bar quality work
- Deprecating alternative GenAI serving paths

## Open Questions

1. The GA scope itself depends on HLR-1's assessment — until it lands, the
   size of the stability and hardening work is an estimate.

# Llama Stack GA-Readiness Assessment

## Description

Resolves the strategy's gating unknown: Llama Stack shipped as Tech Preview,
TP feedback is scattered across support tickets, and no systematic
GA-readiness assessment has been done. This investigation produces the
definitive GA scope — a consolidated inventory of the gaps between current TP
quality and the GA bar across API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, and
error handling — which the stability and hardening work for the GA graduation
is planned against.

## Scope

- Consolidate TP feedback from support tickets into a single reviewed backlog
  of quality signals.
- Assess the current state of the published API surface: versioning status,
  breaking changes across TP releases, and undocumented surface.
- Assess upgrade paths from previous TP releases, including what currently
  breaks or is untested.
- Assess scale limits: what is documented, what is measured, and what is
  unknown.
- Assess error handling coverage on the published API surface.
- Produce the definitive GA scope document: a prioritized gap inventory with
  remediation sizing, stating which gaps are in scope for GA graduation and
  which are deferred, with rationale.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A GA-readiness report exists that inventories gaps in all four assessed
  areas (API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, error handling), with
  each gap traceable to a source (support ticket, code finding, or test
  result).
- The report defines the definitive GA scope: an explicit in-scope vs.
  deferred decision per gap, with rationale.
- The support-ticket feedback corpus has been reviewed end to end, so no
  known TP feedback source is left out of the inventory.
- The report is delivered to the strategy stakeholders for GA scope sign-off.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): "A GA-readiness assessment inventories the gaps between
  current TP quality and GA bar (API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits,
  error handling), producing the definitive GA scope." This epic is that
  assessment.

## Risks / Notes

- Scale-limit verification may require a live cluster or performance
  environment; desk analysis of code, tests, and tickets covers the rest.
- The final GA-scope sign-off is a stakeholder decision informed by this
  investigation's technical inventory.

# Llama Stack API Stability Guarantee and GA Hardening

## Description

Delivers the P0 GA bar for the published Llama Stack surface: versioned APIs
with a published deprecation policy, a tested upgrade path from the last two
TP releases, and remediation of the quality gaps (such as error handling and
scale limits) identified by the GA-readiness assessment. The concrete
remediation scope is finalized against the assessment's definitive GA scope.

## Description of Dependencies

This epic starts once the GA-readiness assessment has produced the definitive
GA scope; its remediation scope may be rewritten to match the assessment's
findings.

## Scope

- Introduce API versioning on the published Llama Stack surface (the
  OpenAI-compatible REST APIs and the LlamaStackDistribution CRD interfaces).
- Author and publish the API deprecation policy for the versioned surface.
- Implement and test the upgrade path from each of the last two TP releases.
- Remediate the GA-bar gaps that the GA-readiness assessment puts in scope
  (error handling, scale limits, and other inventoried gaps), per the
  definitive GA scope.
- Keep the existing Konflux build pipeline for the Llama Stack midstream
  green throughout.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The published API surface is versioned and the versioning is visible to
  consumers.
- The API deprecation policy is published and covers the versioned surface.
- Automated upgrade tests exist and pass for upgrades from each of the last
  two TP releases.
- Every gap the GA-readiness assessment placed in the definitive GA scope is
  remediated in this epic's deliverable or explicitly carried with a recorded
  deferral decision.
- No breaking change to the published surface ships undocumented: any
  unavoidable breaking change follows the new deprecation policy and is
  covered by the tested upgrade path (rollback/compatibility guarantee).
- The existing Konflux build pipeline for the Llama Stack midstream is green
  with the completed change set.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): "Published API surface carries a stability guarantee:
  versioned APIs, deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade path from the last
  two TP releases."
- Additionally executes the gap-remediation scope defined by the
  GA-readiness assessment (the problem statement's "closing the quality gaps
  that TP status currently excuses").

## Risks / Notes

- Size is an estimate until the GA-readiness assessment lands; if the
  definitive GA scope enumerates remediation beyond one sprint of effort or
  spanning distinct surfaces, the work should be split along those surface
  boundaries.

# Llama Stack Production Support Posture

## Description

Puts the production support posture in place that GA requires for Llama
Stack: documented SLO targets, a backport policy, and a supported
configuration matrix. This is support-process and documentation deliverable
work on the Llama Stack component, independent of the stability and hardening
engineering work.

## Scope

- Define and document SLO targets for the supported Llama Stack serving
  surface in GA distributions.
- Define and document the backport policy: which release lines receive fixes
  and for how long.
- Define and document the supported configuration matrix: the deployment
  configurations, provider combinations (e.g. the default inference provider
  and optional vector/RAG providers), and scale envelopes the GA release
  supports, informed by the GA-readiness assessment's scale-limit findings
  where available.
- Socialize the support posture with the supporting organizations and
  product stakeholders for approval.

## Acceptance Criteria

- SLO targets for the GA distribution are documented and published.
- The backport policy is documented and published.
- The supported configuration matrix is documented and covers every
  configuration the GA release supports.
- The support-posture documents are reviewed and approved by the responsible
  support and product stakeholders.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P0): "Production support posture is in place: documented SLO
  targets, backport policy, and supported configuration matrix."

## Risks / Notes

- SLO targets and the backport policy require stakeholder sign-off; the
  engineering deliverable is the documented, reviewed posture itself.

# TrustyAI Guardrails as a Supported Llama Stack Integration

## Description

Promotes safety guardrails via TrustyAI for Llama Stack from an experimental
flag to a supported, documented integration for GA distributions: hardened,
tested against the stabilized Llama Stack API surface, and usable without
experimental opt-in.

## Scope

- Harden the TrustyAI guardrails integration to support standards: error
  handling, configuration validation, and compatibility with the versioned
  Llama Stack API surface and its deprecation policy.
- Remove the experimental-flag gating so the integration is a supported
  configuration in GA Llama Stack distributions.
- Validate guardrails enforcement end to end through the Llama Stack safety /
  provider-plugin surface with TrustyAI as the guardrails provider.
- Add integration-level automated tests running in CI.
- Produce the technically reviewed technical documentation inputs — supported
  configuration, usage, and known limitations — as SME input handed off to the
  GA documentation uplift work; this epic does not author or publish the
  end-user documentation itself.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Guardrails via TrustyAI function in a GA Llama Stack distribution
  configuration with no experimental flags enabled.
- The integration is validated against the versioned, stable Llama Stack API
  surface and follows its deprecation policy.
- Automated integration tests cover the guardrails path and pass in CI.
- The existing Konflux build pipeline for the TrustyAI midstream is green
  with the completed change set.
- The technical documentation inputs (supported configuration, usage,
  limitations) are produced, technically reviewed, and handed off to the GA
  documentation uplift work as SME input — they are not a standalone
  documentation deliverable of this epic.
- Guardrails failure behavior in a supported configuration (no experimental
  flags) is defined and tested: when the TrustyAI guardrails provider is
  unavailable or misconfigured, the failure mode is defined and covered by the
  automated integration tests.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P1): "Safety guardrails via TrustyAI are a supported, documented
  integration (not an experimental flag) for GA distributions."

## Risks / Notes

- This epic consumes the stabilized Llama Stack API surface; it is planned
  after that surface carries its stability guarantee so the supported
  integration targets the GA API, not the TP-era one.

# Dashboard Llama Stack Management Default-On for Entitled Clusters

## Description

Removes the Tech Preview opt-in gate for Llama Stack management in the
Dashboard: on entitled clusters, Llama Stack management is enabled by
default, with no opt-in required.

## Scope

- Change the Dashboard enablement logic for Llama Stack management from
  opt-in to default-on for entitled clusters.
- Handle the entitlement check so clusters without entitlement keep their
  current behavior.
- Preserve a rollback path: enablement remains controllable through the
  existing per-component Dashboard configuration (feature flags / defaults),
  so the default-on can be reverted without a code rollback.
- Update Dashboard tests covering the default-on, entitled, and
  non-entitled paths.

## Acceptance Criteria

- On an entitled cluster with default Dashboard configuration, Llama Stack
  management surfaces without any opt-in action.
- On a cluster without entitlement, Dashboard behavior is unchanged from
  before this change.
- The enablement default is reversible through the existing Dashboard
  configuration mechanism (rollback path verified).
- Dashboard test suites pass, including new coverage for the default-on and
  non-entitled paths.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-5 (P1): "The Dashboard enables Llama Stack management by default for
  entitled clusters (no TP opt-in gate)."

## Risks / Notes

- Release coordination: the default-on flip should ship with the Llama Stack
  GA graduation so TP-quality experience is not exposed by default to all
  entitled users early. This is a release-timing coordination risk, not a
  code dependency — the Dashboard change itself touches only Dashboard
  configuration and enablement logic.

# Llama Stack GA Documentation Uplift

## Description

Uplifts Llama Stack documentation to GA standards, including migration notes
from Tech Preview, so the documented behavior matches the shipped GA
capabilities: the stabilized API surface and deprecation policy, the
production support posture, the supported TrustyAI guardrails integration,
and default Dashboard enablement.

## Scope

Content outline of the documentation work:

- GA-standard documentation for the versioned Llama Stack API surface and
  the deprecation policy.
- Migration notes from Tech Preview, aligned with the tested upgrade path
  from the last two TP releases.
- Documentation of the production support posture: SLO targets, backport
  policy, and the supported configuration matrix.
- Documentation of the TrustyAI guardrails integration as a supported (no
  longer experimental) configuration, including usage and limitations.
- Documentation of default Dashboard enablement of Llama Stack management
  for entitled clusters.
- Removal or replacement of TP-era caveats and disclaimers on surfaces that
  are GA with this graduation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documentation covers all GA capabilities delivered by this strategy's
  implementation work: versioned APIs and deprecation policy, support
  posture, guardrails integration, and default Dashboard enablement.
- Migration notes from Tech Preview are written against the actual tested
  upgrade path and verified against it.
- All documentation is technically reviewed against the implementations it
  describes.
- No TP-era experimental disclaimers remain on surfaces that ship GA with
  this graduation.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-6 (P2): "Documentation is uplifted to GA standards, including
  migration notes from TP."
